claims.text: UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Sudan situation records Total Forcibly Displaced at 11,431,220 (last updated 06 July 2026), comprising 6,597,438 IDPs inside Sudan (last updated 15 June 2026), 273,081 self-relocated refugees in Sudan (last updated 06 July 2026), and 4,560,701 total newly arrived refugees, asylum-seekers and returnees outside Sudan (last updated 06 July 2026).

Re-checked 8 August 2026 via direct fetch: UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Sudan situation now shows 'Total Forcibly Displaced: 11,344,665', labeled 'Last updated 03 Aug 2026' -- up from 11,336,565 (20 July 2026 update). The portal breaks this down as 6,490,949 IDPs within Sudan (last updated 20 Jul 2026), 273,081 self-relocated refugees in Sudan (last updated 06 Jul 2026), and 4,580,635 newly arrived refugees, asylum-seekers and returnees outside Sudan (last updated 03 Aug 2026). UNHCR continues to describe Sudan as the world's largest displacement, humanitarian and protection crisis.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for Sudan (data as of 31 July 2026): 8,685,273 internally displaced persons within Sudan (2.19 million displaced prior to April 2023, 6.49 million since) and 900,819 refugees and asylum-seekers in Sudan; 32% of the refugee/asylum-seeker population is out of camp, 68% is settled in camps.

UN News, 'Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan' (10 August 2026): 'more than nine million people are displaced within the country' and 'more than 30 million people need humanitarian assistance'; fighting in Sirba locality, West Darfur state, has displaced roughly 18,000 people from more than 20 villages since the preceding week, most fleeing across the border into Chad; Sudan's $3 billion humanitarian appeal is only 40% funded ($1.2 billion received). Direct re-fetch of UNHCR's Sudan country page (data.unhcr.org/en/country/sdn) today reconfirms 8,685,273 IDPs within Sudan and 900,819 refugees/asylum-seekers in Sudan, both still labeled 'Last updated 31 Jul 2026' -- unchanged; UNHCR's situation portal remains client-side rendered and its 'Total Forcibly Displaced' figure could not be extracted, and reliefweb.int/country/sdn again returned HTTP 403.
UNHCR describes the Sudan situation as the world's largest displacement, humanitarian and protection crisis.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Sudan situation now shows Total Forcibly Displaced: 11,349,317, labeled 'Last updated 10 Aug 2026' -- up from 11,344,665 (3 August 2026 update). Related widgets, all labeled 'Last updated 10 Aug 2026' unless noted: newly arrived refugees/asylum-seekers and returnees 4,584,868 (of which 3,654,290 newly arrived refugees/asylum-seekers and 930,578 refugee returnees); refugees/asylum-seekers present before April 2023, 837,272; self-relocated refugees in Sudan 273,500. IDPs in Sudan (source IOM/OCHA) remain at 6,490,949, labeled 'Last updated 20 Jul 2026', unchanged.

UN News, 'Sudan war: 200,000 newly displaced as fighting and floods intensify' (19 August 2026), citing IOM: intensifying fighting has displaced at least 200,000 more people since late 2025, with seasonal floods now compounding the crisis. In North Kordofan, fighting and drone strikes on El Obeid's main electrical transformer triggered prolonged power outages disrupting water, health facilities and telecoms; displacement in Sheikan locality rose 25% over eight months, with 200,000+ newly displaced across the wider Kordofan region since late 2025. In Blue Nile, clashes near Geissan displaced 7,800 people, some into Ethiopia. In West Darfur, nearly 18,000 people were displaced in the first half of August. Heavy rain in North Darfur destroyed or damaged about 1,350 shelters in Tawila's camps in the preceding week, displacing 1,000+ families, with further flooding in Kabkabiya and Shangil Tobaya. IOM said a total of 8.6 million people have fled the war since it began in April 2023, and more than 4.5 million people have returned to Sudan in roughly the last 18 months.

ReliefWeb's 'Population Movements from Sudan' report (06 July 2026) corroborates UNHCR's Operational Data Portal total of 11,431,220 forcibly displaced as the most current published figure; no later aggregate total-displaced update had been published as of 17 July 2026.
UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Sudan situation now records Total Forcibly Displaced at 11,336,565 (last updated 20 July 2026), down from the prior 11,431,220 figure (06 July 2026 update).

description: The conflict that erupted in Sudan in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has produced what UNHCR calls the world's largest displacement, humanitarian and protection crisis, forcing millions from their homes inside Sudan and into neighbouring countries. UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Sudan situation last recorded 11,344,665 total forcibly displaced (updated 3 August 2026), comprising 6,490,949 IDPs within Sudan, 273,081 self-relocated refugees in Sudan and 4,580,635 newly arrived refugees, asylum-seekers and returnees outside the country. UNHCR's Sudan country page separately records 8,685,273 internally displaced persons within Sudan and 900,819 refugees and asylum-seekers hosted in Sudan (data as of 31 July 2026). Displacement continues: a 19 August 2026 UN News/IOM alert reported that fighting has displaced 200,000+ more people across the wider Kordofan region since late 2025, with seasonal floods now compounding the crisis in North Darfur, and that more than 30 million people across Sudan need humanitarian assistance while the country's $3 billion appeal is only 40% funded.

impact.summary: UNHCR's Sudan situation portal last recorded 11,344,665 total forcibly displaced (3 August 2026), while its Sudan country page records 8,685,273 internally displaced persons within Sudan plus 900,819 refugees and asylum-seekers hosted there (31 July 2026), with 6.49 million of the internal displacement having occurred since April 2023. UNHCR continues to describe Sudan as the world's largest displacement, humanitarian and protection crisis. A 19 August 2026 UN News/IOM alert reported that fighting has displaced 200,000+ more people across the wider Kordofan region since late 2025 -- including a 25% rise in Sheikan locality displacement over eight months -- and that seasonal floods are now compounding the crisis, destroying or damaging about 1,350 shelters in North Darfur's Tawila camps in a single week; more than 30 million people in Sudan need humanitarian assistance and the country's $3 billion appeal is only 40% funded.

name: Sudan Displacement Crisis

updates.text: UN News/IOM reported (19 August) that fighting has displaced 200,000+ people across the wider Kordofan region since late 2025, including a 25% rise in Sheikan locality over eight months; floods destroyed or damaged about 1,350 shelters in North Darfur's Tawila camps in a week, displacing 1,000+ families, and displaced nearly 18,000 in West Darfur in early August.

UNHCR's Sudan country page (data as of 31 July 2026) recorded 8,685,273 internally displaced persons within Sudan — 2.19 million displaced before April 2023 and 6.49 million since the conflict began — plus 900,819 refugees and asylum-seekers hosted in Sudan.

UN News reported that fighting in Sirba locality, West Darfur, had displaced roughly 18,000 people from more than 20 villages over the preceding week, most of them fleeing into Chad, and put nationwide need at more than 30 million people with Sudan's $3 billion humanitarian appeal only 40% funded ($1.2 billion received).

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal raised the Sudan situation total to 11,344,665 forcibly displaced (updated 3 August 2026), up from 11,336,565 in the 20 July update, with 4,580,635 refugees, asylum-seekers and returnees recorded outside Sudan.
UNHCR's Operational Data Portal revised the Sudan situation total down to 11,336,565 forcibly displaced (20 July 2026 update), from 11,431,220 in the 6 July update.
